title: Short Stuff: Brown-Headed Cowbird
summary: Short Stuff episode on the brown-headed cowbird, a brood parasite that lays its eggs in other birds' nests rather than raising its young. The hosts explain that cowbirds originally followed American bison across the Great Plains, feeding on insects the bison kicked up, which made nest-building impractical. After the bison were overhunted, cowbirds spread into new habitats and adopted cows as perches. They discuss the cowbird's wide host range (including finches, catbirds, yellow warblers), how cowbird hatchlings get a head start and outcompete nestmates, why cowbirds don't imprint on foster parents, and the males' shimmering brown heads and iridescent blue-green plumage. The episode ends with a promotion for a BBC Nature series narrated by David Attenborough.

segments.title: Opening and credits
segments.summary: Josh introduces the short stuff episode and thanks sponsors and listener-suggested topic.

segments.title: Brood parasites and the bison connection
segments.summary: The hosts explain brood parasitism and how cowbirds originally followed American bison across the Great Plains, feeding on insects the bison stirred up and riding on their backs, which made building their own nests impractical.

segments.title: Transition to break
segments.summary: Brief banter about the bison-following behavior before the break.

segments.title: Bison decline and cowbirds switching to cattle
segments.summary: After the American bison were overhunted, cowbirds spread outside their niche; the hosts note Ted Turner's role in bison recovery and say cowbirds later landed on cows, which did not move like bison, yet the birds kept the parasitic habit.

segments.title: Species range and egg size
segments.summary: Five parasitic cowbird species are mentioned, and the brown-headed cowbird is noted as the least picky about host nests, laying eggs even in duck nests, with eggs smaller than the host's eggs.

segments.title: Host defenses and yellow warbler response
segments.summary: The hosts describe how finches may reject the eggs, catbirds puncture or remove them, and yellow warblers build new nests over the eggs, sometimes up to five layers.

segments.title: Cowbird hatchlings outcompete nestmates
segments.summary: Cowbird eggs have a shorter incubation period so they hatch days earlier, letting them push out or outcompete other hatchlings for food, sometimes starving them.

segments.title: Imprinting and cowbird identity
segments.summary: The hosts ask why cowbirds don't take on traits of foster parents; they explain cowbird hatchlings are attuned to adult cowbird sounds, seek out other cowbirds after fledging, and that the mechanism is not fully understood.

segments.title: Where to find brown-headed cowbirds and plumage
segments.summary: Brown-headed cowbirds are found across North America in rural, suburban, and urban areas; males have a shimmering brown head and iridescent greenish-blue body, while females are much less showy.

segments.title: BBC Nature series promotion
segments.summary: Promotion for a new BBC Nature series with David Attenborough, who is 99 and turning 100 in May.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the short stuff episode and the production credit is read.
